name: When is it time to replace a shower instead of just repairing the tile?

mainEntity.name: When is it time to replace a shower instead of just repairing the tile?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should replace your shower when you see chronic grout failure, loose tiles, recurring mold behind walls, or soft flooring near the base. Persistent water stains on ceilings below the bathroom or spongy subfloors around the shower curb indicate hidden moisture damage that topical caulk cannot solve. Surface repairs do not fix failed waterproofing membranes or rotten framing. A complete tear-out allows contractors to repair structural wood, eliminate mold, replace damaged drywall, and rebuild a fully watertight shower system.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace the shower if you notice soft subflooring, loose tiles, chronic leaks into lower levels, or persistent mold, which indicate water has penetrated the wall system.
